newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett rates MOL as "sell".
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett rates MOL as "sell".

text.p: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett rated the shares in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL as "sell" saying they reached a price level which is too high.
"We advise shareholders to sell MOL shares at the current high prices," Tommy Erdei, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett's Budapest-based analyst said.
On Wednesday MOL shares closed at 1,930 forints, up 70. MOL reached an all-time high price of 2,000 forints on May 15.
"The sharp share price increase... was not triggered by any new information concerning the fundamentals of the company," Erdei said.
"Based on our earning forecast MOL's share price is now trading at a price/earnings (P/E) ratio of 12.2 times 1997 earnings," he said.
"This is slightly above the average market P/E. We believe this is unfounded as MOL deserves a discount to the market because of the risk and continued volatility in profits."

The analyst added that the share price rise came on speculation concerning the forthcoming announcement by the government on the attribution of the gas price increases between MOL and the gas distributor companies.
The Hungarian government announced in late November that it would raise retail gas prices by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent.
However, it has remained short of releasing the details, giving way for speculation.

"The market is placing too much faith in rumours that a 16 percent gas price will accrue to MOL and a small balances to the gas distributor companies," Erdei said. "We believe that MOL will only receive 11 to 13 percent of the total increase."

The analyst said that ABN AMRO Hoare Govett's view was influenced by the likely political repercussions of allotting the gas distributors such a small increase in the face of powerful opposition by major foreign investors, some of whom are threatening to sell of their Hungarian investments.
